ROLE You answer the customer's decision question using only the supplied policy passages, decision question, and customer scenario. Do not browse or use outside legal knowledge. TASK Answer the customer's question directly. You may consider all material requirements, prohibitions, exceptions and relevant evidence, and explain them. You are NOT required to construct a separate machine-readable or persistent intermediate rule representation. DECISION REQUIREMENTS - Return YES when the supplied policy and customer evidence establish a positive decision. - Return NO when the supplied policy and customer evidence establish a negative decision. - Otherwise, return NEED_MORE_INFORMATION and identify the facts needed to resolve the decision. - Treat unmentioned facts as unknown, not false. Do not require every fact to be known when the available evidence already determines the outcome. - Pay attention to which person, payment, date or other unit the question covers. If multiple payments may have different eligibility, do not collapse them into an unsupported global conclusion. - Do not presume a specific final answer. Do not make up policy rules or user facts. You may give a concise explanation and cite the supplied passage IDs. - If unresolved, briefly state possible conditional YES/NO answers and what facts make them applicable. This is a conditional explanation, not a persistent rule graph. If definitely decided, use an empty conditional_branches list. - Do not conduct a follow-up conversation. Return one valid JSON object only. OUTPUT SCHEMA { "decision":"YES|NO|NEED_MORE_INFORMATION", "supporting_policy_ids":["E01"], "missing_facts":["specific unresolved fact, only if relevant"], "justification":"brief evidence-grounded explanation", "scope_issues":["if applicable"], "conditional_branches":[{"possible_answer":"YES|NO","conditions_in_words":"applicability condition, only if outcome remains unresolved"}] } === POLICY_PASSAGES === [E01]

You can claim back 25p every time an individual donates £1 to your charity or community amateur sports club (CASC). This is called Gift Aid.

[E02]

You must be recognised as a charity or CASC for tax purposes.

[E03]

The donor must:

[E04]
  • have paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year as you want to claim in Gift Aid
    • [E05]
  • make a Gift Aid declaration that gives you permission to claim it
    • [E06]

    You can claim Gift Aid on donations from individuals. The donor must:

    [E07]
  • have paid the same amount or more in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year
    • [E08]

    You cannot claim on donations:

    [E09]
  • made through Payroll Giving
    • [E10]
  • that are a payment for goods or services or made because your charity or CASC bought goods and services
    • [E11]
  • where the donor gets a ‘benefit’ over a certain limit
    • [E12]
  • of shares
    • [E13]
  • from charity cards or of vouchers, for example Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) vouchers
    • === DECISION_QUESTION === Am I eligible for Gift Aid? === CUSTOMER_SCENARIO === I run a small, independent charity which attempts to help people struggling with their vet costs. I have several people who pay monthly by direct debit and also receive some one off donations. Additional customer information: Robyn Ellis paid the charity £260 on 4 February 2026. The bookkeeping sheet calls it a donation, but January emails show she accepted a £260 price for advertising her grooming salon in the charity's newsletter and on its website. The booking was confirmed after her payment, and the advertisement appeared as agreed. Her separate £20 cash gift in December was unrelated. The charity has an HMRC recognition letter, but Robyn's tax position and any Gift Aid declaration for the £260 have not been checked.
